records.name: Mongolia
records.summary_text:
Mongolia is a country workable for trans visitors. Same-sex activity was decriminalised in 1993, discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is prohibited, and identity grounds were added to the hate-crime provisions of the Criminal Code in 2015. There are no bathroom laws, no border/document friction for foreign passports, and no police targeting pattern; police guidance requires officers to address transgender detainees by their identified gender regardless of identification documents, a favourable enforcement practice.

records.name: Myanmar
records.summary_text: Myanmar is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Section 377 of the Penal Code criminalises same-sex intimacy, and police use “shadow laws” — notably Section 30(d) of the Rangoon Police Act, allowing detention of anyone who cannot “satisfactorily account” for themselves — to target trans and gender-nonconforming people. Since the February 2021 coup the situation has turned lethal: the National Unity Government documented 17 LGBT people killed by mid-2022, and rights groups document arrests, torture, and sexual abuse of LGBT people by junta authorities, with the 2024 Conscription Law
